title: Cruise Ship Pianist Rescued After Nine Hours in the Pacific
summary:
Two fishermen off the coast of California spotted something surprising in the water about 20 miles from shore: a man, treading water, all alone in the Pacific Ocean.

'Yeah, it's a human being. Stop the boat; let's get all of our lines in,' Grant Garrett recalled saying when he and fellow fisherman Sean Norton spotted him.

The man told them he was a pianist on the Ovation of the Seas, a 14-deck cruise ship. He had been in the water for about nine hours. 'The only thing he said to me was, 'Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,'' Norton said.

The fishermen pulled him from the water and called for help. The Coast Guard said it received a report from 'a Good Samaritan who recovered a conscious individual from the water.' The man was handed over to Newport Beach Lifeguards, who confirmed he was an employee of the Ovation of the Seas.

Norton said the man was lucky in one big way: the ocean was unusually warm. The water was 76 degrees Fahrenheit, about 24 degrees Celsius. 'You have this crazy super El Niño year,' Norton said. 'A different year, no way he makes it.'

El Niño is a climate pattern that warms the waters of the Pacific. Scientists monitoring the Pacific say this one is now the strongest on record, with ocean temperatures about 3.05 degrees Celsius above average.

How the pianist ended up in the water is not clear. The cruise line said it would share no further details, 'to respect the privacy of our employee.' What is clear is that two fishermen in the right place at the right time, and a very warm ocean, helped save his life.
why_it_matters: This story shows how being in the right place at the right time can save a life, and how the weather and the ocean can make the difference between danger and survival.
